newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH '97 GRAIN HARVEST SEEN 24.5-24.8 MLN T -GUS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH '97 GRAIN HARVEST SEEN 24.5-24.8 MLN T -GUS.

text.p: Poland's grain harvest will be at 24.5-24.8 million tonnes this year versus 24.9 million tonnes last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said in a preliminary estimate on Friday.
GUS said losses from the recent flooding and bad weather were estimated at 1.4 million to 1.7 million tonnes, of that 0.5 million to 0.7 million tonnes from flooding alone.
GUS estimated the winter grain harvest at 13.4-13.6 million tonnes, 1.5-1.7 million tonnes less than last year.
It estimated winter wheat at six million tonnes, one million tonnes or 14.5 percent less than last year.
It estimated winter rye at 5.6 million tonnes, 0.1 million tonnes or 1.3 percent less than last year.
GUS estimated this year's spring grain harvest at 11.1-11.2 million tonnes, 1.3-1.4 million tonnes higher than last year.
It estimated spring wheat at 2.2 million tonnes, 0.7 million tonnes, or 43.1 percent higher than last year.
It estimated spring barley at 3.3 million tonnes, 0.4 million tonnes or 13.2 percent higher than last year.
Polish grain crops this year have been sown on 8.7 million hectares of land, 64,000 hectares or 0.7 percent more than in 1996, GUS said.
Rapeseed crop had been sown on 300,900 hectares of land versus 282,600 last year, a 6.5 percent difference.
Sugar beet was seen sown on 0.4 hectares of land, 8.2 percent less than last year.
